hook.text: Is Buddhism a religion? It has no creator god. Is football? It has rituals, devotion, and sacred spaces.

buildup.text: Anthropologists struggle to define religion because it takes radically different forms across cultures.

discovery.text: Clifford Geertz defined it as a system of symbols that creates powerful moods and motivations in people.

twist.text: Any definition that fits all religions either becomes too broad (including football) or too narrow (excluding Buddhism).

climax.text: Religion may resist a single definition. Anthropology studies it not by defining it but by observing what it does.

punchline.text: Religion is easier to recognize than to define.

quiz.question: Why is religion hard to define anthropologically?
options: It takes radically different forms across cultures

details.summary: Anthropologists struggle to define religion because no single definition captures its full diversity. Definitions range from belief in supernatural beings to systems of symbols that establish moods and motivations, each revealing different dimensions of religious life.
details.whyItMatters: How we define religion determines what counts as religious. A narrow definition excludes practices like Buddhism or animism. The debate shapes research, policy, and legal frameworks worldwide.
takeaways: No single definition of religion captures all its forms
Definitions shape what scholars study and governments recognize
Functional and substantive definitions highlight different aspects

faq.question: Why is it so hard to define religion anthropologically?
faq.answer: Western definitions often assume belief in a god, but many traditions focus on practice, ritual, or ancestors instead. Any definition broad enough to include all religions risks including everything, while narrow definitions exclude legitimate traditions.

faq.question: What is Clifford Geertz's influential definition of religion?
faq.answer: Geertz defined religion as a system of symbols that establishes powerful moods and motivations by formulating conceptions of existence and clothing them in factuality. This definition emphasizes meaning-making rather than supernatural belief.
